title: Best iPhone 18 Pro Chargers on Amazon UK: What You Need for 60W Fast Charging
pinterest_title: iPhone 18 Pro Chargers: What You Actually Need for Fast Charging
pinterest_subtitle: 60W wired, 25W MagSafe and the charging accessories worth considering in the UK
content_html:
Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max arrive in the UK on 18 September 2026, and charging is one of the first areas where buyers can easily spend money on the wrong accessory. The important change is that the new Pro models can charge much faster than older iPhones, but only when the charger and cable support the right standards.

The short version: if you want Apple's fastest wired charging, look for a USB-C cable rated for at least 60W and a USB Power Delivery 3.1 charger with Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS). If you prefer magnetic charging, the iPhone 18 Pro supports MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging up to 25W.

Why the iPhone 18 Pro charger choice matters

Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max support wired fast charging with a 60W-capable USB-C cable and a USB PD 3.1 power adapter that supports AVS. Apple's own new 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max includes AVS and is the clearest reference point for the new charging system. Apple says that combination can take an iPhone 18 Pro to around 50% in roughly 15 minutes under its test conditions.

That does not mean every charger with a large wattage number will necessarily deliver the same result. A 65W, 70W or 100W charger can have plenty of raw power but still lack the exact AVS profile Apple uses for its fastest charging claim. That is why we would check the protocol support rather than buying on wattage alone.

For wireless charging, Apple lists both MagSafe and Qi2 charging at up to 25W. Apple's current MagSafe Charger can provide that 25W rate when paired with a suitable power adapter.

See Apple's iPhone 18 Pro charging specifications

Our iPhone 18 Pro charging picks

1. Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max - best choice for guaranteed Apple-spec fast charging

If your priority is getting as close as possible to Apple's advertised fast-charge performance, Apple's own Dynamic Power Adapter is the safest reference choice. It is specifically designed to deliver up to 60W dynamically and Apple explicitly states that it supports Adjustable Voltage Supply.

Best for: iPhone 18 Pro buyers who care more about guaranteed protocol compatibility than having several charging ports.

Why we like it: there is no guesswork over AVS support, and Apple specifically lists the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max as compatible.

Worth knowing: it is a single-device charger and the charging cable is sold separately. Amazon availability can vary around a new Apple launch, so check the exact product name and seller before ordering.

Check Amazon UK for the Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max

2. Anker Prime 100W 3-Port GaN Charger - best high-power multi-device option

The Anker Prime 100W charger is a more flexible choice if you want one compact charger for a phone, tablet and laptop. Anker lists up to 100W from a single USB-C port, with two USB-C ports and one USB-A port in total.

Best for: people who want one travel charger for an iPhone plus other USB-C devices.

Why we like it: the 100W output gives plenty of power headroom and the three-port layout is far more versatile than a single-port phone charger.

Important caution: Anker's published specification for this model shows high USB-C output, but its product page does not explicitly advertise AVS. We would therefore buy it for its strong multi-device capability rather than assuming it will reproduce Apple's absolute fastest 15-minute charging claim. Check the latest Amazon specification before purchase if AVS is important to you.

3. Belkin BoostCharge Pro 70W 3-Port GaN - best travel-focused alternative

Belkin's 70W three-port GaN charger is another strong option for travellers. Belkin lists two USB-C ports, one USB-A port, PD and PPS support, interchangeable travel plug tips and compatibility with the iPhone 18 Pro.

Best for: frequent travellers who want a compact charger for several devices and useful plug options.

Why we like it: it combines a sensible 70W ceiling with three ports and broad device compatibility.

Important caution: Belkin's current product page highlights PD and PPS but does not clearly state AVS support. As with the Anker, we would not promise Apple's maximum wired charging speed unless the current Amazon listing explicitly confirms AVS.

Check the Belkin BoostCharge Pro 70W charger on Amazon UK

4. Anker 643 100W USB-C cable - best simple charging cable

A fast charger is only half of the setup. Apple specifies a 60W-capable USB-C cable for the iPhone 18 Pro's fastest wired charging mode. The Anker 643 is rated for up to 100W, so it comfortably clears that cable requirement.

Best for: buyers who need a durable USB-C to USB-C cable with enough power capacity for the iPhone 18 Pro and other devices.

Why we like it: the 100W rating gives useful headroom and the silicone-style construction is designed to stay flexible and resist tangling.

Worth knowing: this is primarily a charging cable. If you need very high-speed data transfer or external-display support, choose a cable designed for those jobs rather than assuming every 100W charging cable has fast data capability.

Check the Anker 643 100W USB-C cable on Amazon UK

5. Apple MagSafe Charger - best for full-speed magnetic charging

If convenience matters more than the fastest possible wired speed, Apple's current MagSafe Charger is the straightforward magnetic option. Apple says it can provide up to 25W wireless charging to compatible iPhone 18 Pro models when paired with an appropriate USB-C power adapter.

Best for: bedside tables, desks and anyone who prefers drop-and-go magnetic charging.

Why we like it: it is Apple's own magnetic charging standard and is explicitly listed as compatible with the iPhone 18 Pro.

Worth knowing: 25W wireless charging is slower and usually less energy-efficient than the fastest wired option. You also need a suitable power adapter; the charging puck alone is not the complete setup.

Check Apple MagSafe Charger options on Amazon UK

6. Anker MagGo 10,000mAh Qi2 Power Bank - best magnetic power bank

The Anker MagGo 10K is a useful portable option if you want magnetic charging away from a wall socket. The Amazon UK listing identifies it as Qi2 certified with up to 15W wireless output and a 30W USB-C port.

Best for: commuting, travel and topping up during long days.

Why we like it: the slim magnetic format is convenient and the 10,000mAh capacity gives significantly more reserve than a very small emergency battery.

Worth knowing: this model's wireless output is 15W, so it does not take advantage of the iPhone 18 Pro's full 25W Qi2 ceiling. Think of it as a portability pick rather than the fastest charging option.

Check the Anker MagGo 10K on Amazon UK

7. Anker 20,000mAh 87W Power Bank - best high-capacity wired power bank

If you care more about capacity and wired charging than magnetic convenience, this Anker 20,000mAh model is the more practical travel companion. The Amazon listing shows up to 87W total output, two USB-C connections, USB-A and a built-in USB-C cable.

Best for: flights, long journeys and people carrying several devices.

Why we like it: 20,000mAh is a substantial capacity for a portable battery and the integrated USB-C cable means one less cable to remember.

Worth knowing: a power bank's maximum headline output does not automatically mean the iPhone will draw that full figure. Charging speed depends on the USB PD profiles negotiated between the phone and power bank.

Check the Anker 20,000mAh 87W Power Bank on Amazon UK

Which charger should you buy for the iPhone 18 Pro?

If you want the fastest Apple-supported wired charging: look first at Apple's 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max plus a cable rated for at least 60W. The reason is simple: Apple explicitly confirms AVS support on that adapter.

If you want one charger for several devices: the Anker Prime 100W and Belkin BoostCharge Pro 70W are more versatile because they offer multiple ports. Just check the current listing for AVS if reproducing Apple's peak iPhone charging result matters to you.

If you mainly charge overnight or at a desk: MagSafe is easier to live with and the iPhone 18 Pro can now accept up to 25W wirelessly.

If you travel a lot: a wired power bank gives you better charging efficiency, while a magnetic battery is more convenient for quick top-ups without a cable.

Three mistakes to avoid

1. Buying on wattage alone. A 100W label does not by itself guarantee Apple's fastest iPhone charging mode. Protocol support matters.

2. Reusing an old low-power cable. The charger may be capable of 60W or more, but the cable also needs to support sufficient power.

3. Assuming every magnetic charger is 25W. Many perfectly good Qi2 power banks and charging pads are still 15W models. Check the actual wireless output before buying.

Our verdict

The iPhone 18 Pro makes high-speed charging much more useful, but it also makes the specifications more important. For buyers who want the simplest route to Apple's fastest charging, the official Dynamic Power Adapter is the most straightforward choice. For households with laptops, tablets and multiple phones, a good multi-port GaN charger is more useful overall, even if you should verify AVS support before expecting Apple's maximum charging figure.

For most people, our practical setup would be a quality multi-port USB-C charger, a 100W-capable USB-C cable and either a MagSafe charger or a power bank depending on how often you charge away from home.
